abstract: This Anthropic Economic Index report analyzes AI adoption patterns across geographies and enterprises using Claude usage data from 1 million conversations and API traffic. The study finds that AI adoption is geographically concentrated in high-income countries and technologically advanced economies, with per-capita usage strongly correlated with GDP per capita globally (0.7% increase in Claude usage per 1% GDP increase) but more weakly in the US (1.8%). Enterprise deployment shows automation-dominant patterns (77% of API use versus 50% of Claude.ai use), with businesses primarily automating coding and administrative tasks rather than engaging in collaborative human-AI augmentation.
keyFindings: AI adoption is highly geographically concentrated, with small technologically advanced countries (Israel at 7.0x, Singapore at 4.57x) leading in per-capita usage while emerging economies show minimal usage (Nigeria at 0.2x, India at 0.27x).

Global Claude usage per capita is strongly positively correlated with income, with a 1% increase in GDP per working-age capita associated with a 0.7% increase in Claude usage per capita across countries.

Within the US, DC leads in per-capita Claude usage at 3.82x population share, followed by Utah at 3.78x, with disproportionate focus on document editing, job applications, and information provision tasks.

Enterprise API usage is 77% automation-dominant compared to 50% augmentation on Claude.ai, concentrated in coding tasks (representing roughly half of API traffic with 6% for debugging and 5% for AI system development).

High-adoption countries show more collaborative human-AI augmentation patterns while low-adoption economies show greater tendency toward task automation, even when controlling for task mix differences.
methodology: Analysis of 1 million randomly sampled Claude.ai conversations from August 4-11, 2025 across 150+ countries and all US states, combined with first-party API traffic analysis using privacy-preserving classification methods. Geographic data derived from IP address geolocation, with privacy filters excluding cells with fewer than 15 conversations and 5 unique user accounts (500 conversations and 250 accounts for request clusters). Tasks classified using O*NET taxonomy and bottom-up clustering. Correlation analysis conducted between Claude usage and GDP per capita; automation/augmentation patterns analyzed with and without controlling for task composition using partial regression analysis. US state data uses minimum 100 observations threshold; global country data uses minimum 200 observations for statistical reliability.
qualifiers: Analysis limited to IP-address-based geolocation which may not capture VPN usage; authors note uncertainty in measures for low-usage countries in random sample and acknowledge that Utah's high usage may be partially associated with coordinated abuse though robustness checks suggest this is not driving results. Data reflects Claude.ai Free and Pro conversations and first-party API customers only, not broader AI adoption. Geographic usage patterns only available for Claude.ai traffic, not enterprise API usage. O*NET taxonomy is US-based and may not capture all international task variations. Causality between income and adoption cannot be determined from correlation analysis. Privacy filters may miss some lower-frequency tasks or regions. Authors note this is preliminary analysis of early adoption patterns and that 'more research is needed' to understand whether automation growth reflects model capability improvements versus user learning-by-doing.
